cohort: The study included 172 pregnancies in 123 women at risk of PA-VTE who received thromboprophylaxis with enoxaparin at National Women's Hospital, Auckland, New Zealand.
finding: Standard doses of enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis were effective at preventing PA-VTE (1.2% breakthrough VTE rate), but high rates of postpartum hemorrhage (36.6% >=500 mL, 9.3% >=1000 mL) were observed in the cohort, suggesting higher doses may increase bleeding complications.
mod_finding: Neuraxial analgesia/anesthesia was used in 52.4% of births, including 39.6% of vaginal births, and higher doses of enoxaparin may limit access to this mode of pain relief during labor and birth.
